, partnered with Instant Hydration to launch their subscription program in September 2024. This Austin-based hydration brand built early success on one-time purchases but realized they were leaving growth and predictability on the table without recurring revenue. In less than 90 days with Skio, they transformed from zero recurring revenue to subscription-first business.

Instant Hydration launched in 2024 targeting $5.5M annual revenue through direct-to-consumer hydration products. The Austin-based brand built early momentum on one-time purchases, but by mid-2024, the team faced the classic DTC reality: living off transactions is a treadmill.

Every month started at zero. Every repeat customer had to be re-acquired. Rising CAC pressure made profitability harder without repeat orders, and customer loyalty remained at risk with no incentive for buyers to stick around.
Matthew Holman and the team realized they needed a business model transformation—converting casual buyers into loyal repeat customers while building dependable recurring revenue streams.

Instant Hydration's transaction-only model was creating unsustainable growth dynamics. No recurring revenue stream meant zero foundation of predictable income. Rising paid acquisition costs pressured profitability without repeat orders driving lifetime value.

Customer loyalty remained fragile—one-time buyers had no reason to return, making churn inevitable. The brand was stuck in constant re-acquisition mode instead of building compound growth through retention.

During Black Friday/Cyber Monday, the platform processed thousands of new subscriptions in just days. Multiple six-figure subscription revenue days proved the model was both scalable and profitable, with November activations hitting 85% higher than September baseline.
in subscription revenue
58% of total revenue
The transformation was complete in one quarter. Subscriptions grew from zero to 58% of total revenue (up from 38% baseline), creating durable recurring income where none existed before.

Instant Hydration proved that transactional brands can transform into subscription powerhouses in a single quarter. From zero recurring revenue to subscription-first business model with tens of thousands of active subscribers.
Subscriptions shifted from add-on feature to core business foundation driving predictable revenue growth.

Everyday Dose launched in 2020 with flagship product targeting customers looking to optimize energy and health without coffee jitters. Based in Miami and targeting $33M+ annual revenue, the brand quickly built passionate customer base through organic social media sharing and referrals.
Their Previous Platform Was Bleeding Revenue Through Data Loss

Everyday Dose's subscription setup was hemorrhaging money through mysterious technical failures that cost the cash-strapped startup real revenue. Customers' stored credit card information would mysteriously disappear, causing payment failures that meant active subscribers weren't getting billed and orders weren't shipping.

Login nightmares compounded revenue losses. Subscribers faced broken login links, 404 error pages, and an unintuitive interface when trying to manage orders. Many gave up and contacted support for minor changes.

Reliable performance eliminated the bizarre bugs completely. Payments processed reliably, customer data stayed secure, and the subscriber portal simply worked. Panicked emails from customers about login failures or duplicate charges virtually disappeared.
Lower churn and higher satisfaction drove more subscribers staying longer, boosting recurring revenue while time savings translated into creative marketing moves bringing new customers.

William Hicks knew this from day one. As Co-Founder and President, he was tasked with building a subscription foundation that could scale with their ambitious growth plans. The San Francisco-based brand was targeting $10M+ in annual revenue, and subscriptions would drive the majority of that growth.
Their Previous Platform Was Bleeding Revenue and Burning the Support Team

For a subscription-first brand, this wasn't just embarrassing. It was revenue at risk. Every rejected card meant lost MRR. Every bad shipment eroded trust. Customers expecting a clean, functional portal got friction instead.
Migrating subscription platforms keeps founders up at night. Thousands of recurring payments on the line, one wrong move, and revenue vanishes overnight.
Stage 3: Full subscriber transition. The final step ported over the entire subscriber base and monthly payments. Zero downtime. Zero angry customers. Zero lost revenue.
Revenue Protection Through Platform Partnership
Conversion improvement: Streamlined funnel boosting acquisition rates
Clean Labels, Clean Revenue Model

Transparent Labs built its reputation on a promise most supplement companies won't make: full-disclosure labeling, clinically dosed ingredients, no proprietary blends. Every formula is third-party tested. Every ingredient is listed at its exact dosage. In an industry built on vague claims and hidden fillers, that transparency became the product itself.

The product wasn't the problem. Transparent Labs had strong product trust and high repeat-purchase intent. But the system around the subscription wasn't built to capture that intent at scale, and every gap meant revenue walking out the door quietly.

And that baseline started reinforcing growth. Each saved subscriber stayed in the billing base, continued generating future revenue, and reduced reliance on new acquisition. Over time, those effects stacked. What began as incremental improvements evolved into a system where gains hold, improvements build on each other, and impact increases as the program scales.
